newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt paper prices up on low sales proceeds.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt paper prices up on low sales proceeds.

text.p: Prices of Russian government paper rose on Thursday on cheap interbank roubles and low Finance Ministry proceeds from Wednesday's auctions, dealers said.
They forecast prices would rise further in the next few days with a possible correction in short-term paper.
*Average yield fell to 18.74 pct from 19.29 pct on Tuesday
*Turnover rose to 5.16 trln rbls from 3.07 trln rbls
*Banks transferred 3.82 trln rbls to the trading
*Central Bank sold 780 bln rbls of T-bills, OFZ bonds and VSM railway bonds
"The Finance Ministry and the Central Bank got about 400 billion (roubles) less then they needed to repay," said Aljba-Alliance Bank dealer Mikhail Vasilyev.
"It has not happened for a long time, that's why people were in for active trading today. As a result the yield fell on all paper."
The Finance Ministry raised 7.87 trillion roubles on Wednesday's government paper auctions and repaid 8.29 trillion roubles worth of Treasury bills.
Bank Menatep dealer Andrei Grechishnikov said cheap rouble funds on the interbank market pushed government paper prices up.
Roubles with tomorrow delivery fell to 5,788-90 per dollar from 5,782-83 at Wednesday's close. Overnight credits were 1-6 percent after 2-7 percent.
